descriptionChirho: The core Hifil meaning of שׁלך: physically throwing, casting, or hurling an object or person — into water, a pit, fire, onto the ground, etc. Arabic أَلْقَى/طَرَحَ, Korean 던지다, Spanish arrojar/lanzar, Swahili -tupa, Hindi फेंकना/डालना.

Metaphorical casting away — rejecting, discarding, or abandoning a person, relationship, or moral standard; often in pleas not to be abandoned by God or exhortations to discard idols/sin. Korean 버리다 (discard), Spanish desechar (reject), Hindi त्यागना (abandon).

Forceful downward throwing — casting down in judgment, hurling to the ground, throwing down from a height; connotes violence, divine judgment, or forceful removal. Korean 내던지다 (fling down)/떨어뜨리다 (cause to fall), Spanish derribar (knock down), Hindi गिराना (topple), Swahili -angusha (cause to fall).

Expelling or driving out from a place or presence — casting out of a land, territory, or domain; distinct from mere physical throwing by the emphasis on removal/banishment. Korean 내쫓다 (expel/drive out).

The Hofal (causative passive) of שׁלך: being thrown, being cast out, being hurled — the subject is the one thrown rather than the thrower. Arabic مَطْرُوح (thrown, passive participle)/طُرِحَ (was thrown), Korean 던져지다 (be thrown), Swahili -tupwa (be thrown).
